preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is an integer between 2 and 100 inclusive.
The input contains exactly n-1 edges defining the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices within the valid range [1, n].
The input edges form a valid tree (connected and acyclic).

postconditions.description: The output strictly follows the specified format: number of paths, followed by path descriptions containing length, edge indices, start vertex, target vertex, and distance x.
The set of selected paths covers every edge of the tree exactly once (pairwise edge-disjoint and union is the set of all edges).
Every vertex in the tree belongs to at least one of the selected paths.
For each path, the specified edge exists in the path, the start and target vertices are the endpoints of that edge, and the distance x is in [0, 1].
The generated array of maximal stopwatch times (res) is lexicographically minimal among all valid solutions, meaning res[1] is minimized, then res[2], and so on.
